exercise.name: Incline Twisting Sit-up

reference.title: Incline Twisting Sit-up
reference.listing: Video (title and number from the catalog listing; the page could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

equipment: Decline bench (slant board with ankle roller)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl and sit up, inhale as you lower under control.
breathing.cadence: About 1.6 s up, a short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.tempo: About 1.5 s up, brief pause, 2 s down
prescription.progression: Steeper board, slower lowering, then a light load

cues.text: Lie on the inclined board head-down, feet hooked under the roller, fingertips lightly behind the head, elbows wide.
Breathe out, tuck the chin a little and curl the head and shoulder blades off the board.
Keep curling and sit up, turning the trunk so the left elbow heads toward the right knee.
Pause in the twist; alternate sides on the next rep.
Breathe in and roll back down slowly: low back first, then the shoulder blades, head last.
Rest the shoulders on the board for a moment; repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Twisting only the neck or the elbows
mistakes.fix: Turn the chest; the head follows.

mistakes.mistake: Yanking the head with the hands

mistakes.fix: Twist gently and stay within a comfortable range.

kinematics.measure: Trunk (pelvis to C7) from the board
kinematics.norm: From lying on the board to sitting up, turned toward one knee (clinical opinion)
Low back curls early and stays rounded at the top (clinical opinion)
Most of the second half of a sit-up is hip flexion (Andersson 1997)
A moderate twist at the top (clinical opinion)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.

Lying head-down raises pressure in the head; skip the decline with uncontrolled high blood pressure, glaucoma or a recent eye or head problem (clinical opinion), and sit up slowly at the end of the set.
Check that the roller is locked and the feet are hooked before lying back.
Full sit-ups load the low back more than curl-ups (McGill 1998; Axler and McGill 1997).
Osteoporosis or vertebral fracture: avoid repeated loaded spinal flexion and twisting.
Disc problems: avoid combined loaded flexion and twisting (McGill 1998).
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Neck pain: cross the arms on the chest.
Low-back discomfort: stop at a crunch.

muscleNotes.obliques: The twist at the top brings in the external oblique of the left side and the internal oblique of the right side (clinical opinion); obliques were active in the sit-up (Escamilla 2016; Konrad 2001).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis curls the trunk off the board (Escamilla 2016).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris pull the trunk up (Andersson 1997).
